What to say: Apply online at sftreasurer.org/business within 30 days of starting business in San Francisco. outcomes.original: Filing step: File the fictitious business name (DBA) statement with the San Francisco County Clerk if the public-facing restaurant name differs from the legal entity name, then publish the statement in a court-approved newspaper once a week for four weeks. What to say: Bring the completed FBN form and photo ID to the County Clerk's office (City Hall, Room 168) or mail it with a check for the filing fee (approximately $60–$120). After filing, publish the statement in a San Francisco newspaper (e.g., the San Francisco Examiner or the San Francisco Chronicle) once a week for four consecutive weeks, then file the affidavit of publication with the Clerk within 45 days. Banks and the building permit application will require the filed FBN statement.

outcomes.original: Filing step: Apply for the Public Health Permit to Operate a food facility after the DPH plan check is approved, a certified food safety manager is on staff, and the space is ready for final inspection. What to say: Apply online through the DPH Environmental Health portal at least one month before the target opening date, entering the BAN, Location ID (LIN), and federal EIN. Pay the $470 Permit to Operate application fee (FY 2026–27 schedule; includes the initial inspection). Schedule the pre-opening inspection when the space is at least 80% complete—all equipment installed, surfaces sealed, hot water flowing, and a certified food safety manager certificate on file. Book the final inspection at least two weeks in advance. The permit is issued after the final inspection confirms the facility matches the approved plans.

outcomes.original: Estimated time: 120 to 300 days. Estimated government cost: $3,100 to $5,500. Notes: The day and cost ranges cover the Conditional Use Authorization and the Health Permit to Operate, the two approvals in the entitlement path, and reflect the time to approval when those approvals are granted (not the time to a denial or withdrawal). The CUA timeline is estimated at 120–300 days from filing to Planning Commission hearing and final approval based on typical San Francisco hearing timelines for neighborhood commercial conditional use cases; the single comparable CUA in the candidate set (1988.272C at 2642 Ocean Ave) took 45 days in 1988, but that pre-dates current environmental review, neighborhood notification, and hearing-scheduling procedures. The health permit takes 14–45 days after plan check is complete and prerequisites are met. The cost range includes the CUA filing fee (approximately $3,100 for a use decision without construction in 2024, CPI-adjusted annually per the Planning fee schedule), the health permit application fee ($470 for FY 2026–27), and the plan-check fee ($828–$2,207 for a new restaurant depending on complexity, FY 2026–27 schedule). Total estimated government fees for the two approvals are $4,400–$5,700. Building permit fees ($800–$15,000) are not included because the building row has insufficient-information status, but they will add materially once the change-of-use determination is made. State and federal registrations (EIN, Secretary of State, seller's permit) add $70–$150 and take 1–10 days but are prerequisites, not approvals in the entitlement path.
